# Orion MIS

> Orion MIS is a British technology house based in Chichester, West Sussex.
> We design, build and program our own warehouse automation: the Helix parcel
> sorter, the HeliOS warehouse control software, conveyors and controls, all
> made in the UK under one roof. Orion is the manufacturer, not a reseller of
> third-party sorters.

Key facts:

- Founded 2019. About 40 people, all designing and building in the UK.
- Helix is a modular pivot-wheel parcel sorter. It sorts on a 200 mm gap,
  is built in 200 mm modules, and has up to 20,000 parcels per hour of
  single-line capacity. It handles boxes, bags, tyres and non-conveyables.
- On a live UK parcel hub, a Helix line running HeliOS went from 4,500 to
  13,000 items per hour at peak.
- HeliOS is Orion's own warehouse control software, written alongside the
  hardware: parcel tracking, device control, a live 3D twin of the site, and
  faults located by device, door and code in real time.
- Three ways to buy: pay per parcel, pay monthly, or buy outright. The first
  two need no capital expenditure. Per-parcel rates are agreed per site,
  based on volume and parcel mix.
- Order to go-live in as little as six weeks; every line is built and tested
  in Orion's factory before it ships.
- Two years parts and labour warranty as standard.
- Two years of Helix installs are on order.
- Customers are UK parcel centres, couriers, 3PLs and fulfilment operations.
- Contact: info@orionmis.co.uk · book a call at https://orionmis.co.uk/call
- Press and media: https://orionmis.co.uk/press

## Insights

- [All insights & guides](https://orionmis.co.uk/insights): the hub for every
  Orion guide — engineering-led, no gated PDFs
- [Cross-belt vs tilt-tray vs wheel sorters](https://orionmis.co.uk/parcel-sorter-comparison):
  how the three parcel sortation technologies work, honest strengths and
  weaknesses, and how to choose on destination count, parcel mix, footprint
  and budget
- [What does warehouse automation cost in the UK?](https://orionmis.co.uk/warehouse-automation-cost-uk):
  2026 cost guide — entry systems from ~£4,000/month financed, a worked
  £320.9k sorter example with 4-month payback, hidden costs and install
  timelines
- [Print & apply labelling systems: a UK buyer's guide](https://orionmis.co.uk/print-and-apply-labelling-guide):
  how print & apply works — print engine, tamp/blow/wipe applicators,
  verification scanning — a buyer's checklist, and the ten Amazon SLAM lines
  as proof
- [The real cost of manual parcel sortation (UK, 2026)](https://orionmis.co.uk/cost-of-manual-sortation):
  the wage-bill maths of a manual sort line at £16.30/hr all-in, the invisible
  costs of agency, overtime and rework, and what the same money buys in
  automation
- [How long does warehouse automation take to install?](https://orionmis.co.uk/warehouse-automation-installation-time):
  UK timelines phase by phase — conveyor packages 6–10 weeks to site, full
  sortation 6–25 weeks order-to-live, on-site install under 4 weeks, and the
  order-by dates for peak
- [Powered roller vs belt conveyors](https://orionmis.co.uk/powered-roller-vs-belt-conveyors):
  how the two conveyor families work, where each honestly wins,
  zero-line-pressure accumulation explained, and why most real systems mix
  both
